[Date]
Crestline Mutual Insurance
[Insurance Address]

Re: Appeal for Claim CLM-771043 
Patient: Darnell Hutchins 
MRN: 49327 
DOS: 2026-05-11 
CPT: 81445 

Dear Claims Review Department,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of claim CLM-771043 for the genomic profiling test (CPT 81445) performed on Mr. Darnell Hutchins on May 11, 2026. The claim was denied under code CO-55, indicating that the procedure was deemed experimental/investigational.

However, according to Crestline Mutual's medical necessity criteria, comprehensive tumor gene-panel testing is a covered indication for metastatic non-small-cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) to direct targeted therapy. Mr. Hutchins has been diagnosed with stage IV metastatic NSCLC adenocarcinoma, and the genomic profiling was ordered per NCCN guidelines to identify actionable alterations in EGFR, ALK, ROS1, and KRAS before initiating first-line therapy.

The clinical documentation from the oncology note dated May 8, 2026, confirms the necessity of this testing, as it is essential for guiding treatment decisions in Mr. Hutchins's case. The test results are critical for determining the most effective therapeutic approach for his condition.

We kindly request that you reconsider the denial based on the provided clinical necessity and payer policy guidelines. Please find attached the relevant clinical documentation and a summary of the medical necessity assessment.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. We look forward to your prompt response.

Sincerely,
[Your Name] 
[Your Title] 
[Your Contact Information] 
[Your Practice Name] 
[Practice Address] 

Attachments: Clinical Documentation, Medical Necessity Assessment Summary

Dear Claims Review Department,  

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of claim CLM-771043 for CPT code 81445 (solid tumor gene-panel sequencing) for my patient, Darnell Hutchins, who has been diagnosed with stage IV non-small-cell lung adenocarcinoma. The claim was denied based on denial code CO-55, indicating the service was deemed experimental/investigational.  

According to Crestline Mutual's medical necessity criteria, comprehensive tumor gene-panel testing is recognized as a covered indication for metastatic NSCLC to guide targeted therapy. This aligns with the clinical documentation supporting the necessity of this testing, as outlined in the oncology note dated 2026-05-08, which confirms the pathology of metastatic NSCLC adenocarcinoma and the need for genomic profiling to identify actionable alterations before initiating first-line therapy.  

The CPT code 81445 was billed in accordance with the guidelines, and the clinical necessity for this testing is well-supported by the NCCN guidelines. The assessment of medical necessity confirms that the testing is essential for directing appropriate treatment options for Mr. Hutchins.  

I kindly request a reevaluation of this claim based on the provided documentation and the payer's policy regarding genomic profiling for metastatic NSCLC. Please find attached the relevant clinical documentation and medical necessity assessment for your review.  

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your prompt response.  

Sincerely,  
[Your Name]  
[Your Title]  
[Your Contact Information]  
[Your Facility Name]  
[Facility NPI]  

Attachments: Clinical Documentation, Medical Necessity Assessment.
